newsitem.title: CANADA: Interfor seeks gains in operating net.
newsitem.headline: Interfor seeks gains in operating net.

text.p: International Forest Products Ltd said Thursday it hopes to boost its operating earnings by C$59 to C$65 million a year through changes it expects will take effect over the coming 12 months.

Retiring chief executive William Sauder told the forestry company's annual meeting said that of the total C$15 million would come from efficiencies in the company's logging operations, C$15 million from its new cedar mill, C$15 million from a new whitewood mill and C$14 million or more from higher pulp-related income.
Sauder said analysts were forecasting Interfor's earnings at C$0.25 to C$0.50 a share for 1997. "I hope we will be there, in that range," he told reporters after the meeting.
Interfor earlier announced a first-quarter profit of C$0.09 a share.
Sauder said Interfor hopes to build a new whitewood mill to replace its Mackenzie Seizai operation in 1998 if the company's profits strengthen.

Interfor's goals are to return to profitability so it earns a 10 percent return on invested capital, to maintain an investment-grade credit rating and to fund from cash flow capital projects that make operations more efficient.

Joining a chorus of other British Columbia forest company chiefs, Sauder said heavy government-imposed logging costs made the industry's position precarious and lead to inadequate financial returns. "This cannot continue. It's unsustainable," he said.

Environmental protestors attacked the company at the meeting, accusing it of violating British Columbia's strict logging code. Interfor disputed the accusations and pledged its commitment to maintain a strong environmental record.
After several spirited exchanges with environmental and native American critics, Sauder closed the meeting.
